# Chapter Two: Daily Grind

The alarm went off at 5 AM as it did every day. Victor, rolled over and kissed his wife, who wouldn’t be up for another two hours, the baby still slept in the room with them and had been up for a few hours the night before. The kids also wouldn’t be starting their day for at least the same amount of time, but as with every weekday, work was calling and as every morning he thought about calling in sick, but he needed the paycheck more then he needed the time off.

He took a shower and then wiped the steam from the mirror and there looking at himself was an older version of the young man he remembered, a little heavier, but not too heavy to be considered fat but the grey in his chest hair and sneaking its way into his temples and with brown hair it was easier to see the grey, he had kept himself clean shaven for at least 5 years since he had first seen the signs of grey snaking through his beard, hoping to stave off the look of age for as long as possible. But the chest grey and the laugh lines on his face gave away his 37 years of life. “A little older but still kicking my friend” he said to himself in the mirror. He had thought about dying his hair but his wife always winced at that and told him she liked the grey, it made him look distinguished, he thought she was full of shit, but didn’t have the heart to disregard her on this so he never had done it.

He pulled the newly pressed Khaki Park Police uniform from the plastic that the dry cleaners seem to always put them in and put it on, smoothing out the creases, he then pulled on the tactical boots that he had shined the night before and admired the polished look of them before moving over to the closet, pulling his gun from the locker he kept in the closet a Nickel Plated.38 revolver with a 6 inch barrel and black Hogue grips, Jessica never liked him having a gun in the house, but it was part of the job, they had agreed he could as long as he kept it locked up when at home. He strapped his backup to his leg another 3-inch barrel.38, lord knows why he carried either, he had never had to shoot someone in anger and even the drunks in the park had never given him too much trouble.

He had been assigned duty at the C&O Canal, Maryland Side for going on 10 years now it was a good job and he liked it, just he would have liked it more if it paid better, with two kids and living in this part of Maryland it wasn’t cheap. He left house he had barely been able to afford in the suburbs of Gaithersburg, near the lake forest mall, back when they bought the place, once he had gotten assigned here, Gaithersburg had been a nice up and coming area. Now it was a good place to live but with Germantown and Frederick the new hotspots, it was beginning to look a bit aged. He got into his 91 Toyota Celica and pulled out of the driveway it wasn’t much to look at but it was paid for and allowed him the ability to afford the car payment on Jessica’s Sienna Van, which since it was for the kids it allowed him to justify it, without getting too depressed. Long since had the days of cools sports cars passed him by, He still had his aged Harley Softail in the garage, but he rarely got time to ride it and Jessica had been on him since the birth of their first child to get rid of it, every time she heard a story or saw a news report of someone getting killed on a bike, the old argument would reignite itself. But he always stood his ground and hence had won that argument repeatedly.

He always tried to get out early traffic on 270 was hell if you had too late of a start. He merged onto the highway from Middlebrook road and started his daily trip. Everything was as normal until he hit Macarthur Blvd. Traffic shouldn’t have been this heavy but the closer he got to the great falls entrance the more he realized that traffic was almost at a standstill. It took Vic an hour to reach the gatehouse, Johnny who worked the late shift was still manning the gate, turning everyone away. Vic rolled down the window, “hey man what’s going on?” he asked as he noticed all of the unmarked, marked and park police vehicles lined in the lot. Johnny was about 25 and his short cut blonde hair with the ever present sun burn when his hat as off was a good joke to most of the guys who worked with him, the curse of the Irish they would say to him good naturedly.

Vic continued to stare at the vehicles in the lot “Oh man Vic, they have been asking for you for like an hour man, you need to get to the visitor hall now, isn’t your cell phone on? Which of course it wasn’t Vic usually turned it on when he got to work just to avoid the early morning bill collector calls. Vic looked confused, “Who has been asking for me” Johnny just shook his head, “the old man, and he is not happy” Shit Vic thought Captain Robert Shilling “The Old Man” as everyone called him was a hard ass who liked to run things like he was still in the marine corps, personally he hated Vic and well the feeling was mutual, if The Old Man was asking for him, it was definitely not going to be a good day. “I don’t know what happened but something big is going on.” He waived Vic in, and as he pulled past the litany of cars he noticed federal plates, State Police, Local Police quite a few Park Police vehicles and a limo, which seemed very out of place Vic pulled his old Celica in next to the limo, made sure to turn on his cell phone which immediately said he had 10 voice mails, probably all from the Captain and his Mounty cap from the passenger seat.

He didn’t know what he had done but the old man was the Sr. Officer here and if he was being asked for then he was probably in trouble. Vic had a bit of an issue with authority, but he had been able to keep a lid on it mostly and had only been in trouble a hand few a times. But this sounded like something big.

As he walked into the visitor center which had seemed to become a impromptu command post there was a Hodge podge of people, State police, guys in suits, park police and yes Priests. He didn’t know what they were doing here but this really wasn’t good. Seemed to be arguments over something and of course there were some snippets of conversation over who had jurisdiction over this. This was a mess, that much Vic knew and he was about to be put into the middle of it. It was going to be a very bad day.

He didn’t get two steps before his name was called and everyone turned to see who had entered. Vic sighed and turned “Sir, what’s up” he walked over to the group in the corner which consisted of two priests and two guys in suits. As Vic approached he saw the familiar wide shoulders and blonde hair and realized he knew the priest, well the younger one and his mouth just about fell open. “Vic, you are being assigned to the father here” The old man said and from the look on his face he was not happy about it, the old man still wore that high and tight haircut and kept himself fit, hell you could bounce a quarter off his stomach that matched with the wide shoulders, starched uniform and boots that were practically mirrors, he was the vision of a retired Marine Officer. Vic was a little confused, he looked between the suites and the priest, He was at a loss, he had no idea what a couple of clergy were doing here, or what the hell was going on, but the day just got better and better. “Does someone want to fill me in, I am feeling a little at a loss” he said trying to get a grip on himself.

The old man’s bushy eyebrows came together to form that uni-brow that everyone joked he got when angry shook his head. “As of 3:30 this morning what was left of a body washed up on the shore of the canal not 3 miles from here, it was discovered by a patrolman and called in, within two hours we had these guys”, he pointed to the suites “from the Justice department and these guys” pointing at the priests “from the Vatican, apparently the Justice Department has Jurisdiction, and the Vatican sent these guys as consultants. So now you know as much as I am allowed to. Within an hour of going through our records, they pulled your name out and said they wanted you as their liaison. So congratulations, you are now assigned to the Justice Department” Said the Captain using that booming baritone he liked to show off to anyone within ear shot.

What the fuck, was all Vic thought, he looked at his old friend who was dressed complete with black suite and white collar and figured that’s why he got pulled for this duty, Sam wanted a friendly face.

The younger priest held out his hand “Hey Vic” Vic smiled and took it, “Sam, I would have never thought to see a Jesuit priest at a murder scene, I am guessing you had something to do with this little assignment” Father Lawrence looked a bit sheepish “I apologize after going through the files Bishop Talbot here picked you but since we knew each other, it didn’t hurt, how are you, still attending church?” he asked innocently Vic just shook his head “Jessica takes the kids on Sunday, I try not to if I can help it, no offense, just we agree to disagree about certain topics” he said looking into his old friends eyes and seeing the sadness, I am sorry about the loss of your parents I am I know it’s been ages since we were choir boys at St Marks, but I understand your reservations.”

Vic looked around at all the suits “So you want to tell me what a couple of priests are doing at this little shin dig” He could see his friends eye shift, Vic knew that look from when they were kids, it’s something he did when he wasn’t being truthful, he could never lie very well “We are here as consultants on the case, it might be ritualistic in nature” Okay Vic decided to leave it alone, so since I guess I am here to lias, what’s my duties. Bishop Talbot stepped up and introduced himself “Mr. Handy I am Sr. Bishop Talbot, I see you know my young colleague The bishop extended his hand and Vic shook it, “Sir, I am not sure what you think I can do that the Captain can’t I am sure he would be a better choice as a liaison then myself” Vic said looking towards the Captain and seeing that same stern look he always had. “No son I think you are exactly who we need” and the Bishop left it at that. “You will be our guide while here as well as interface with the Park and local police on our behalf should we need to, Smith and Park here will be our federal liaison’s with Justice” Vic nodded it almost sounded like the priests were in charge. Which would be a lot weirder then things already were, he was about to say something that would probably have earned him quite the disciplinary action until. Sam, who knew him all too well sensed what was coming saved him “Well let’s go see the site shall we”. Sam grabbed His friend by the arm and gently led him out of the building before he could speak another word. And the procession went outside into the morning sun. The park was eerily empty and aside from police cars the lot was absent of the usual runners and bikers who so frequented the park on a daily basis. The precession walked over to two Gator’s that were parked near the visitor center and the drivers Vic knew as fellow park officers, seemed quiet and a little pale in the face, His guess was this was not the first lot to visit the site and that didn’t speak well for what he was going to see.

They rode along the path of the canal for about two or three miles and as they pulled up to the area Vic could see police tape setup as well as a crime lab van from Rockville as well as some State Police cars. They unpacked themselves from the Gator’s and while they waited for their escort Vic took a moment to scan the area, As he was looking towards the far side of the canal he thought he could see two people in the woods near the banks, Must be hikers doing a little rubber necking he thought and dismissed it. Bishop Talbot walked up behind Vic and laid a hand on his shoulder. “Father Lawrence tells me you served in the military young man” He looked back at the Bishop and nodded 11 Bravo infantry, I was Airborne he said and then looked away hopefully the Bishop taking the hint he didn’t want to talk about it anymore. Unfortunately, he didn’t “I hear you served overseas, see any action” Vic sighed, it was going to be one of those days. “Not a lot sir, I was at Camp Casey Korea and aside from a little small arms fire, not a lot was going on” Vic walked forward the Bishops hand slipping from his shoulder as he rushed a little both to get away from the older man and to catch up to his friend.

He leaned into Sam “Couldn’t you guys have found someone else for this gig Sam, I mean you’re not doing me any favors here, the amount of paperwork alone is going to have me cursing your name for a month” Father Lawrence just shook his head, “Sorry Vic, it wasn’t my call the bishop insisted it had to be you, not sure why but I couldn’t talk him out of it, he saw your name and then he made a few calls, after that even your boss couldn’t talk him out of it” Vic found that a little odd, “Who did he call?” Sam just shook his head, not sure, but Vic saw that look again, His friend was holding something back, he would have to get him alone and find out what all this mystery was, well once they got through this.

They approached the site of the body and Vic stopped in his tracks, pieces of bone and intestine were strung at least 50 feet up the shore along with an arm and from what he could tell, what was left of a leg “Jesus, what kind of monster would do this” he whispered Sam visibly flinched “Why would you say that” he asked defensively. Vic looked at him and shook his head, “Really, you think a sane man would do this to a person, hell I would have thought a bear or something just from the fact this guy looks ripped apart”.

“A bear would have eaten more of the body and not left a lot of the intestine strewn, nor would it have spread the carcass so far along the short” came a baritone voice from behind Vic which damn near made him jump out of his skin. He turned to come face to face with a man who had to be a head taller than Vic himself and since Vic was 6 feet even that was saying something. The man’s full beard had a small amount of grey but his eyes were what really bothered Vic, they were a slate blue and seemed to stare right through you. He was wearing a pair of jeans and a flannel shirt and looked more like a lumberjack then a cop. “Excuse me” Vic said The man just smiled “A bear would have eaten most of this and kept it in a smaller area, this body wasn’t eaten, it was torn apart and then strewn here to be found, more like a statement then a prey kill, Edgar Johnson, I am here with his eminence as there animal expert” and Edgar held out his hand, You must be Victor Handy Vic took the hand and it was a strong grip, but not too strong “I am, but what would a couple of priests need with an animal expert” he asked realizing this was just getting weirder and weirder.

Edgar scanned the remains and walked a few feet only stopping once or twice to take a glance at something. “this was a trophy kill, it was left for us to find almost like a marker, they wanted to get someone’s attention, just not sure who” he said rubbing his beard as he thought. “It was almost like it knew…” that was as far as he got before the Bishop cleared his throat and shot him a look. It didn’t escape Vic but he didn’t mention it, just filed it away. There was more to this than anyone was letting on. He would have to grill his old friend because if they threw him in the middle, he sure as shit wasn’t going to walk around blind. And why choose him anyway, this made no sense, this whole day in fact had too many questions than answers for his liking. “Do you mind if I take a quick look at the remains Sam” he asked his old friend. Same glanced at the Bishop who apparently gave his consent with a barely noticeable nod. “Go ahead, but be careful we don’t want evidence tainted”.

Vic made his way under the police tape taking notice that Edgar and the Bishop were in somewhat of a heated debate. He was not liking this at all. He had never actually worked a murder so wasn’t sure what he was looking for, But he had seen dead bodies though not quite in this bad of a condition. He looked closely at what he assumed was a torso, there were tear marks made from something large, like a knife but in a pair of 4 consecutive marks. “Now that’s a bit odd” he said to himself more than anyone else. There was no way a person could have done this much damage to a body and those tear marks were too big for a bear. He was in over his head and he just wanted to know how much shit he was in.
